ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Jack London

code.originalText: Twelve-week review: kidney function after the SGLT2 inhibitor, urine albumin, liver tests, AUDIT, mood, safety and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Mr. London has had no alcohol for eight weeks. He has taken dapagliflozin for two weeks with a little more passing of urine and no dizziness, genital symptoms or illness, and has not needed the sick-day rules. He takes losartan 100 mg, naltrexone, thiamine and vitamin D3 every morning. His home readings average 120/76. He writes every morning and has started a new novel; he swims or rides in the late morning. He would like to stop smoking in the new year. He asks what the next months hold for his kidneys. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 122/78, pulse 70; weight 80.9 kg, BMI 27.0
Regular rhythm; no edema; no fall in blood pressure on standing

Tiredness, ankle swelling and high blood pressure (158/98 mmHg) with a raised creatinine (1.98 mg/dL, eGFR 43) and albumin in the urine (240 mg/g), found at intake; a creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL at an insurance examination about fourteen months ago, by his account; chronicity and cause under evaluation with a nephrology consultation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented kidney damage found in 1913; superseded when the consultation staged chronic kidney disease.

Chronic kidney disease, stage G3b A2 (eGFR 42 to 43, urine albumin 240 mg/g), most likely from hypertension with a contribution from two years of daily naproxen; kidneys of normal size, without stones or obstruction; urine sediment bland; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented kidney disease

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to his documented kidney damage and death from uraemia; the cause in the modern episode is synthetic and is not a claim about his real kidneys.
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, untreated until intake
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation.

Alcohol use disorder, severe (seven DSM-5-TR criteria): a bottle of whisky or more most days for years, a morning drink to steady his hands, failed attempts to cut down, and drinking despite knowing it harms his health; AUDIT 27; PEth 410 ng/mL
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his own published account of heavy drinking; the criteria, scores and amounts are synthetic and are not a claim about his real drinking.
Alcohol-associated fatty liver without advanced fibrosis (liver stiffness 7.2 kPa; steatosis on ultrasound); FIB-4 2.28 at intake
S — Synthetic finding of the ultrasound and elastography at the consultation; not a claim about his real liver.
Daily self-directed naproxen for knee and back pain for about two years, stopped at intake; acetaminophen in its place
S — Synthetic medication history; the joint pain is anchored to the documented rheumatism of 1914, which is not given a diagnosis.
Cigarette smoking, about ten a day; not ready to stop while he stops drinking
S — Synthetic tobacco use; a physician-author's suggestion of heavy tobacco use is recorded only as a retrospective claim.
Right ankle sprain (lateral ligaments, moderate), from stepping into a burrow while walking the pasture; Ottawa ankle rules negative; healed in about four weeks
S — Synthetic acute injury; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Chronic kidney disease G3b A2 (N18.32). eGFR 40, from 44, two weeks after dapagliflozin: the expected early dip of about 9 percent, well within the 30 percent accepted; potassium 4.7 mmol/L. Urine albumin 96 mg/g, down 60 percent from 240. Stage G3b A2. [S]
Continue losartan 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg.
Creatinine, eGFR, urine albumin and potassium in three months, then twice a year; calcium, phosphate and PTH in six months.
Nephrology review in three weeks, three months after the consultation.

Hypertensive chronic kidney disease (I12.9). 122/78 by standardized measurement, close to a systolic target below 120. [S]
If systolic stays above 120 at three months, add amlodipine 5 mg.

Alcohol use disorder, severe, in early recovery (early remission needs three months without criteria) (F10.20). Eight weeks abstinent with PEth 6 ng/mL; liver tests and MCV normal. AUDIT 9 for the past three months. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm, firearms locked, 988 card carried. [S]
Continue naltrexone for at least a year.
Counseling every two weeks from now.
PEth every two to three months.

Cigarette smoking (F17.210). Ready to set a quit date in the new year. [S]
Nicotine patch with a short-acting form, or varenicline, at the next visit.
